title: An open box folded from a sheet of cardboard

stimulus.title: An open box
stimulus.html:
A packaging designer makes an open box from a rectangular sheet of cardboard 3030 centimeters long and 2020 centimeters wide. She cuts a square with sides of xx centimeters from each corner and folds up the sides. The table gives the volume V(x)V(x) of the box, in cubic centimeters, for selected values of xx.
Volume V(x) of the open box, in cubic centimeters, for cut size x, in centimeters
xx (centimeters)123
V(x)V(x) (cubic centimeters)5048321008

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Write an expression for V(x)V(x), the volume of the box, in terms of xx.

rubric.point: A correct product of the three dimensions
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(30 - 2x)(20 - 2x)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: After the cuts, the base is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30 - 2x</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20 - 2x</annotation></semantics></math> centimeters and the height is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> centimeters, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(30 - 2x)(20 - 2x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Use your expression to find the cut size xx that gives the greatest volume, and the greatest volume. Give your answers correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: Both values correct to three decimal places, with units
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.924</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 3.924</annotation></semantics></math> centimeters and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1056.306</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V \approx 1056.306</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters

parts.sample: Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x(30 - 2x)(20 - 2x)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < x < 10</annotation></semantics></math> and use the maximum feature: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.924</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 3.924</annotation></semantics></math> centimeters gives the greatest volume, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1056.306</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V \approx 1056.306</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of VV on the interval [1,3][1, 3], with units. Explain what this value represents on the graph of VV.

rubric.point: The value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>252</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">252</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters per centimeter, identified as the slope of the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, V(1))</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, V(3))</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1008</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>504</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1008 - 504}{3 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>252</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 252</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters per centimeter; it is the slope of the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>504</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 504)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1008</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 1008)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{V(3) - V(1)}{3 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1008</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>504</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1008 - 504}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>252</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 252</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters per centimeter. It is the slope of the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>504</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 504)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1008</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 1008)</annotation></semantics></math> on the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the secant line from part B(i) to estimate V(2)V(2).

rubric.point: An estimate from a point on the secant line

parts.sample: The secant line is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>504</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>252</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 504 + 252(x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> it gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>504</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>252</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>756</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">504 + 252 = 756</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>756</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(2) \approx 756</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is the estimate in part B(ii) an overestimate or an underestimate of V(2)V(2)? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Underestimate, with a reason from the concavity of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: underestimate, because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>, so the graph is above the secant line there

underestimate: the average rates on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 2]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>328</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">328</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>176</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">176</annotation></semantics></math>, decreasing, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: An underestimate. On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down: the average rates of change on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 2]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>328</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">328</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>176</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">176</annotation></semantics></math> cubic centimeters per centimeter, which decrease. So the graph lies above the secant line on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math>, and the secant line's value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>756</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">756</annotation></semantics></math> is below <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>832</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V(2) = 832</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: The designer uses the model VV only for values of xx that make sense in this context. Explain what the largest possible value of xx is, and why the model cannot be used past it.

rubric.point: The bound <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 10</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 10</annotation></semantics></math>) with a reason from the dimensions of the sheet
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 10</annotation></semantics></math>, because the width <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20 - 2x</annotation></semantics></math> must be positive; at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 10</annotation></semantics></math> the cuts use the whole <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>-centimeter width

for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 10</annotation></semantics></math> the model uses a negative width <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20 - 2x</annotation></semantics></math>, so its values (negative on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 < x < 15</annotation></semantics></math>) describe no real box

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> must be less than <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>. The box's width is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20 - 2x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 10</annotation></semantics></math>: the corner squares would use the whole width of the sheet, leaving no box. Past <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 10</annotation></semantics></math> the model uses a negative width (and gives negative volumes for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 < x < 15</annotation></semantics></math>), which no real box has, so the context limits the domain to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < x < 10</annotation></semantics></math>.
